en: Although often depicted in a duel, historical records do not confirm that Lapu-Lapu personally struck the fatal blow against Ferdinand Magellan.
Many believe Emilio Aguinaldo made the first Philippine flag, but he only designed it while Marcela Agoncillo and her daughter sewed it.
Although Jose Rizal is the national hero, Emilio Aguinaldo, not Rizal, served as the first president of the Philippine Republic.
Although many think the Philippines always celebrated independence on June 12, President Macapagal officially changed the holiday from July 4 in 1962.
Despite common beliefs that the Katipunan was exclusively male, women like Gregoria de Jesús and Marina Dizon actively served as full members.
Many assume the Philippine eagle lives everywhere, but it is critically endangered and restricted to the forests of Mindanao, Luzon, Samar, and Leyte.
Many mistakenly call the waling-waling the national flower, but the sampaguita officially holds the title of the Philippine national flower.
Tagalog is not the sole native language, as the Philippines actually has over 180 distinct indigenous languages, including Cebuano, Ilocano, and Hiligaynon.
Contrary to some historical periods, the current 1987 Philippine Constitution strictly limits the president to a single six-year term without reelection.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were not built by Spanish colonizers, but were instead carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
The lyrics of the Philippine national anthem were originally written in Spanish by José Palma, not in English or Tagalog, before being translated later.
Unlike House representatives who serve specific districts, the 24 Philippine senators are elected by the entire voting population of the whole country.
